cards.back: $P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$. Total probability over a partition $\{A_i\}$: $P(B)=\sum_i P(A_i)P(B\mid A_i)$ — the denominator of Bayes' theorem.
Independent: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$, $P(B\mid A)=P(B)$. Mutually exclusive: $P(A\cap B)=0$ (can't co-occur). IID = independent + identically distributed.
$P(h\mid D)=\frac{P(D\mid h)P(h)}{P(D)}$. Posterior = Likelihood × Prior / Evidence. $P(h)$ prior, $P(D\mid h)$ likelihood, $P(D)$ evidence, $P(h\mid D)$ posterior.
$h_{MAP}=\arg\max_h P(D\mid h)P(h)$ ($P(D)$ dropped). $h_{ML}=\arg\max_h P(D\mid h)$. They coincide when the prior is **uniform**.

cards.front: Bayesian justification of the version space
cards.back: Uniform prior + 0/1 consistency likelihood ⇒ $P(h\mid D)=1/|VS_{H,D}|$ for consistent $h$, 0 otherwise. Any consistent hypothesis is a MAP hypothesis (justifies Find-S / Candidate-Elimination).
Even a 98%-sensitive test on a rare disease (prior 0.008) gives only $P(cancer\mid+)\approx0.21$ → MAP = ¬cancer. Posterior depends strongly on the prior (base rate).
Assumes features conditionally independent given the class. $v_{NB}=\arg\max_{v_j} P(v_j)\prod_i P(a_i\mid v_j)$. Learning = counting frequencies (no search).
Full joint: $k(v^n-1)+(k-1)$ — exponential in $n$. Naïve Bayes: $k\,n(v-1)+(k-1)$ — linear in $n$. Independence makes it tractable.
Gaussian (continuous features ~ normal), Multinomial (discrete counts, e.g. word counts), Bernoulli (binary present/absent features).
An unseen value → $P=0$ → whole product 0. Fix: add-1 (Laplace) $P(a_i\mid v_j)=\frac{c+1}{n+k}$, or m-estimate $\frac{n_c+mp}{n+m}$.
Multiplying many small probs underflows to 0. Work in **log space**: $\arg\max[\log P(v_j)+\sum_i \log P(a_i\mid v_j)]$ — products become sums.

$v_{OB}=\arg\max_{v_j}\sum_{h_i} P(v_j\mid h_i)P(h_i\mid D)$ — posterior-weighted vote over ALL hypotheses. Lowest possible error; the winning class need not be the MAP hypothesis's choice. Infeasible to compute.
Pick ONE hypothesis at random ∝ posterior $P(h\mid D)$, classify with it. Bound: $E[\text{err}_{Gibbs}]\le 2\,E[\text{err}_{Bayes\ optimal}]$.
Under independent zero-mean Gaussian noise, $h_{ML}=\arg\min_h \sum_i (d_i-h(x_i))^2$. Squared-error minimization IS maximum likelihood.

For latent variables. **E-step:** estimate expected hidden values (responsibilities) given current params. **M-step:** re-estimate params by ML using them. Increases likelihood each step → local optimum.
E-step: posterior that each sequence used coin A; attribute heads fractionally. M-step: $\theta_A'=\frac{\text{expected heads from A}}{\text{expected flips from A}}$. Repeat to convergence.
GMM = **soft** clustering (probabilistic membership), **elliptical** clusters via $\Sigma$, fit by EM. K-Means = hard, spherical. K-Means ≈ special case of GMM.

E-step responsibility: $\tau_j(x_i)=\frac{\pi_j\mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_j,\Sigma_j)}{\sum_k \pi_k\mathcal{N}(\cdots)}$. M-step: $\mu_j,\Sigma_j$ = responsibility-weighted mean/covariance; $\pi_j=\frac1n\sum_i\tau_j(x_i)$.
$P(q_n\mid q_1\dots q_{n-1})=P(q_n\mid q_{n-1})$ — future depends only on present. Chain $\lambda(\pi,A)$: initial dist $\pi$, transition matrix $A$ (rows sum to 1).
$P(Q)=P(q_0)\prod_t P(q_t\mid q_{t-1})$. Estimate: $\pi_i$ = fraction of sequences starting in $i$; $a_{ij}$ = (count $i\to j$)/(count out of $i$).

cards.front: HMM parameters λ = {Q, Σ, π, A, B}
cards.back: Q hidden states, Σ observation alphabet, π initial dist, A transition matrix $a_{ij}=P(q_{t+1}=j\mid q_t=i)$, B emission matrix $b_j(o_k)=P(o_t=o_k\mid q_t=j)$.
Assumptions: Markov (state depends on prev state) + output independence (obs depends on current state). Problems: 1 Likelihood (Forward), 2 Decoding (Viterbi), 3 Learning (Baum-Welch).

$\alpha_t(j)=P(o_1\dots o_t,q_t=j\mid\lambda)$. Init $\alpha_1(j)=\pi_j b_j(o_1)$; recurse $\alpha_t(j)=[\sum_i \alpha_{t-1}(i)a_{ij}]b_j(o_t)$; terminate $P(O\mid\lambda)=\sum_j \alpha_T(j)$. $O(N^2T)$.

$\beta_t(i)=P(o_{t+1}\dots o_T\mid q_t=i)$; $\beta_T(i)=1$; $\beta_t(i)=\sum_j a_{ij}b_j(o_{t+1})\beta_{t+1}(j)$. Product $\alpha_t(j)\beta_t(j)$ = prob. of being in state $j$ at $t$ given the full $O$.
Brute force sums over $N^T$ paths ≈ $(2T+1)N^T$ ops (exponential). Forward DP: $O(N^2T)$.

Most-likely path $Q^*$. $\delta_t(j)=\max_i[\delta_{t-1}(i)a_{ij}]b_j(o_t)$; back-pointer $\psi_t(j)=\arg\max_i[\delta_{t-1}(i)a_{ij}]$. Terminate at $\max_j\delta_T(j)$, backtrack via $\psi$. Forward uses Σ; Viterbi uses max.

$\gamma_t(j)=\frac{\alpha_t(j)\beta_t(j)}{P(O\mid\lambda)}$ = prob. in state $j$ at $t$. $\xi_t(i,j)=\frac{\alpha_t(i)a_{ij}b_j(o_{t+1})\beta_{t+1}(j)}{P(O\mid\lambda)}$ = prob. of edge $i\to j$ at $t$.
$\hat a_{ij}=\frac{\sum_t \xi_t(i,j)}{\sum_t \gamma_t(i)}$; $\hat b_j(k)=\frac{\sum_{t:o_t=k}\gamma_t(j)}{\sum_t \gamma_t(j)}$; $\hat\pi_i=\gamma_1(i)$. Baum-Welch = EM for HMMs.
Local optima (use restarts); underflow of α/β → use log space; #hidden states chosen by validation likelihood / domain knowledge; states have no intrinsic meaning.

**State** = hidden situation type (e.g. weather), follows the Markov chain. **Observation** = visible symbol emitted by the state (e.g. mood), governed by emission probs B. Emissions are probabilistic, capturing real-world variability.
